question: What lie did you tell as a kid that spiraled way out of control?
story: When I was nine I told my class my uncle owned a water park, and by spring my teacher had scheduled a field trip there. I did not have an uncle. I had a man named Rick who dated my mom for one summer and once took us to a public pool. But I said water park, and thirty kids believed me instantly, and for four months I was the most important child in that building. Kids saved me seats. A boy gave me his good markers. Then the permission slips went home. Actual paper. Actual buses. I panicked so hard I told my mother I had a stomach bug for nine straight days. Here is how it ended. She found the slip in my backpack, read it twice, and did not yell. She just drove me to school and made me tell everyone myself. Twenty two years later my mom still introduces me at parties as her daughter, the water park heiress.
